note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set.

checkers.alarm: max |row_sum(out) - target| > (64*log2(n_vars)+128+2*k_max)*eps*target (eps of the output dtype; row sums in float64) or a non-finite output. (k_max = largest number of stored entries in a row; sequential row sums accumulate error ~ k*eps.)
checkers.invariant: After normalisation every such cell has the same total count, equal to target_sum (or the median of the original non-zero cell totals when target_sum is None).
checkers.observation_point: After _normalize_total_helper returns, with a snapshot of the input taken before it.
checkers.precondition: Finite non-negative float or integer count matrix (dense, CSR, CSC), exclude_highly_expressed=False, cells with positive total. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Cell totals lie within the range of the input dtype. Each judged cell's size factor (usable total / target) is a normal float of the output dtype, and the target sum is at least finfo(dtype).tiny/eps of the output dtype (normalised entries are not subnormal). Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Depth equalisation is the purpose of library-size normalisation; unequal totals bias every downstream comparison.

checkers.alarm: target (or, when None, the common value) lies outside [sum over certainly-retained genes, + ambiguous genes] by more than (64*log2(n_vars)+128+2*k_max)*eps*target. (k_max = largest number of stored entries in a row; sequential row sums accumulate error ~ k*eps.)
checkers.invariant: The genes that are not highly expressed (documented: no cell has more than max_fraction of its total counts in the gene) sum to target_sum in every cell with a positive retained total; with target_sum=None they are equal across cells. Ambiguous genes widen the retained sum to an interval [certain, certain+ambiguous].
checkers.observation_point: After _normalize_total_helper returns.
checkers.precondition: Finite non-negative data, exclude_highly_expressed=True, at least one gene that is certainly retained (entries within 1e-5 relative of the max_fraction threshold are ambiguous and bounded by an interval). Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Cell totals lie within the range of the input dtype. Each judged cell's size factor (usable total / target) is a normal float of the output dtype, and the target sum is at least finfo(dtype).tiny/eps of the output dtype (normalised entries are not subnormal). Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Otherwise the size factor was computed on a different gene set than the one the documentation promises.

checkers.alarm: max |N(2X) - N(X)| > 64*eps*max|N(X)| or max |f(2X) - 2 f(X)| > 64*eps*max|2 f(X)|.
checkers.invariant: Normalising 2*X yields the same matrix as normalising X and size factors that are exactly doubled (counts scaled by sequencing depth carry the same composition).
checkers.observation_point: After _normalize_total_helper returns; the helper is re-called on 2*snapshot with all arguments forwarded.
checkers.precondition: Explicit target_sum, finite non-negative float data, any exclude_highly_expressed/max_fraction. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Cell totals lie within the range of the input dtype. Each judged cell's size factor (usable total / target) is a normal float of the output dtype, and the target sum is at least finfo(dtype).tiny/eps of the output dtype (normalised entries are not subnormal). Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Scaling all counts of a cell by a constant is a pure depth change and must not alter normalised expression.

checkers.alarm: max |N(dense) - N(csr)| or the size-factor difference exceeds (64*(log2(n_vars)+2)+2*k_max)*eps*max|.|. (k_max = largest number of stored entries in a row; sequential row sums accumulate error ~ k*eps.)
checkers.invariant: Dense and CSR storage of the same values give the same normalised matrix and size factors.
checkers.observation_point: After _normalize_total_helper returns; the helper is re-called on the other representation.
checkers.precondition: Finite non-negative float data, any target_sum, exclude_highly_expressed and max_fraction (no entry within 1e-5 relative of the exclusion threshold). Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Cell totals lie within the range of the input dtype. Each judged cell's size factor (usable total / target) is a normal float of the output dtype, and the target sum is at least finfo(dtype).tiny/eps of the output dtype (normalised entries are not subnormal). Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: A scientific result must not depend on whether a matrix is stored sparsely.

checkers.alarm: |var - 1| > 2*64*eps*(1+mean_in^2/var_in)*(log2(n_obs+2)+n_obs/32) or (zero_center) |mean| > 64*eps*(1+mean_in^2/var_in)*(log2(n_obs+2)+n_obs/32), computed in float64 from the produced values (the library variance is a one-pass sum of squares accumulated recursively over n_obs cells, error up to ~eps*n_obs*(1+mean^2/var)).
checkers.invariant: Scaled genes have sample variance (ddof=1) 1 over the observations used for the statistics, and mean 0 when zero_center=True.
checkers.observation_point: At return of scale_array.
checkers.precondition: Finite data, n_obs >= 2 over the rows used, max_value=None, genes with finite positive input sample variance (squares and their sum within the normal range of the input dtype), any storage and mask. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Numeric (float or integer) storage dtype. Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: z-scoring is only meaningful if the output actually has unit variance and zero mean.

checkers.alarm: max |clipped - min(unclipped, max_value) (/max(.,-max_value))| > 64*eps*max(1,max|unclipped|).
checkers.invariant: The clipped output equals the unclipped output truncated at max_value (and at -max_value when zero_center=True); nothing else changes.
checkers.observation_point: At return of scale_array; scale_array is re-called with max_value=None on a snapshot of the input.
checkers.precondition: max_value given, finite data; genes whose unclipped scaling is non-finite (e.g. a constant gene) are not judged. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). max_value > 0. Numeric (float or integer) storage dtype. Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Winsorisation must only cap extreme z-scores.

checkers.alarm: any outside-mask entry changed or max |inside - scale(subset, same container; CSR for sparse input with zero_center=False, as the masked path converts CSC to CSR)| > 64*eps*(1+mean^2/var)*(log2(n+2)+n/32)*max(1,max|scale(subset)|) (n = masked cells, recursive accumulation).
checkers.invariant: Observations outside the mask are unchanged; observations inside equal the unmasked scaling of the masked subset alone.
checkers.observation_point: At return of scale_array; scale_array is re-called on the masked subset.
checkers.precondition: A mask that selects some but not all observations, finite data; genes that are numerically constant within the masked subset are not judged (their standard deviation is rounding noise). Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Numeric (float or integer) storage dtype. Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Documented: the mask restricts both the derivation of scaling parameters and the scaling itself.

checkers.alarm: Any cell total (or the matrix total) differs from min(original, target) (exact integer comparison). For float dtypes, a total within one ulp of the input dtype of the target is not an alarm.
checkers.invariant: Afterwards each cell total (or the matrix total) equals min(original, target).
checkers.observation_point: At return of downsample_counts, with a snapshot of the input.
checkers.precondition: Non-negative integer-valued counts, any replace, either counts_per_cell or total_counts. Float counts: every entry that may hold the reads is below the dtype consecutive-integer limit (2^24 for float32); integer dtypes: the target fits the dtype; boolean storage holds at most one read per entry. Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Downsampling exists to equalise depth without creating or losing more reads than requested.

checkers.alarm: A negative or non-integer entry, an entry that was 0 and is not, or (replace=False) an entry larger than the original.
checkers.invariant: The result is non-negative and integer-valued, zero entries stay zero, and with replace=False no entry exceeds its original count.
checkers.observation_point: At return of downsample_counts.
checkers.precondition: Non-negative integer-valued counts, any replace. For integer dtypes with replace=True, each cell's target count does not exceed the dtype maximum. Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Drawing reads from the observed multiset cannot create reads for unobserved genes or (without replacement) exceed observed counts.

checkers.alarm: |D_k . r_j| / (||D_k|| ||y_j||) > 64*eps*cond(D)^2*max(1,sqrt(n_obs)) (eps of the data dtype; normal-equation error model, n-term inner-product rounding).
checkers.invariant: Each gene's residual is orthogonal to every column of D (linear dependence removed, residual mean 0).
checkers.observation_point: Before regress_out stores its result; compared with a snapshot of the input.
checkers.precondition: Numeric keys, design D=[1, keys] of full column rank with cond(D) <= 1e6 (raw, unscaled D), non-constant genes with max|y| >= finfo(dtype).tiny/eps (dtype of the data). Dense input is not self-overlapping (no two entries share memory, e.g. a writeable sliding_window_view): the routine writes in place, so aliased entries make its result undefined.
checkers.rationale: Regressing out a covariate must remove its linear influence on the expression.

checkers.alarm: |mean(z)| or |std(z) - 1| > 64*eps*(1+|avg|/dev)*(log2(m+2)+m/32) for a bin of m genes (the library's bin mean/std is a streaming groupby reduction).
checkers.invariant: Within each mean bin the normalised dispersions have mean 0 and sample std (ddof=1) 1.
checkers.observation_point: After dispersions_norm is computed.
checkers.precondition: Flavor seurat; mean bins holding at least 2 finite dispersions with positive spread and no infinite (overflowed) dispersion.
checkers.rationale: Normalised dispersion is defined as a within-bin z-score; deviating bins distort gene ranking.

checkers.alarm: |median(z)| or |mad(z) - 1| > 64*eps*(1+|med|/mad)*(log2(m)+2).
checkers.invariant: Within each mean bin the normalised dispersions have median 0 and normalised MAD 1 (same robust estimator).
checkers.observation_point: After dispersions_norm is computed.
checkers.precondition: Flavor cell_ranger; mean bins holding at least 2 finite dispersions with positive MAD.
checkers.rationale: Robust normalisation by bin is the Cell Ranger definition of normalised dispersion.

checkers.alarm: means/dispersions/normalised dispersions differ by more than 64*eps*(1+|v|)*(log2(L+2)+L/32) with L = max(n_obs, n_vars) (recursive accumulation over cells, bin statistics over genes) (for dispersions and normalised dispersions additionally multiplied by the gene's one-pass-variance conditioning 1+mean^2/var, computed on the values the flavor uses) (for normalised dispersions |v| is replaced by |v|+(|disp|+|bin centre|)/bin spread*(2+|v|)), different NaN pattern, or the highly_variable mask differs when no two finite normalised dispersions tie and the n-th and (n+1)-th scores differ by more than that tolerance and n_top_genes does not exceed the number of scored (non-NaN) genes.
checkers.invariant: The result with that batch_key equals the result with batch_key=None.
checkers.observation_point: After the per-gene table is assembled; the unbatched computation is re-run on the same AnnData.
checkers.precondition: flavor seurat or cell_ranger; batch_key has exactly one populated category; every gene expressed in at least one cell. Genes within a bin are separated from the bin centre by more than the rounding of the dispersion. The reference is computed on the cells with a non-missing batch label (the cells the batched selection uses), and needs at least two of them. The selection comparison applies only when no bin of two or more genes has zero dispersion spread.
checkers.rationale: Batch-wise selection over a single batch must be the plain selection.

checkers.alarm: An unselected gene strictly outranks a selected gene lexicographically on (highly_variable_nbatches, dispersions_norm), or too few genes are selected.
checkers.invariant: Every selected gene ranks at least as high as every unselected gene on (nbatches,) normalised dispersion, and at least min(n_top_genes, #finite) genes are selected.
checkers.observation_point: After the per-gene table is assembled.
checkers.precondition: n_top_genes given, flavor seurat or cell_ranger, expressed genes (mean != 0).
checkers.rationale: Selecting the top n genes must pick the genes with the highest score.

checkers.alarm: An unselected gene strictly outranks a selected gene on the documented key, or the number selected differs from min(n_top_genes, n_vars).
checkers.invariant: Selected genes outrank unselected genes on the documented key (rank ascending then nbatches descending; paper variant nbatches descending then rank ascending; NaN rank last) and exactly min(n_top_genes, n_vars) genes are selected.
checkers.observation_point: After highly_variable is assigned.
checkers.precondition: flavor seurat_v3 or seurat_v3_paper.
checkers.rationale: The v3 HVG definition is a ranking; the flagged set must follow it.

checkers.alarm: decrease > (64*(sqrt(n_vars)+log2(n_vars))+4*n_vars)*eps, value > 1 + that slack, value at n_vars differing from 1 by more than it, or non-finite.
checkers.invariant: Cumulative proportions are non-decreasing in n, lie in [0,1], and equal 1 at n = n_vars.
checkers.observation_point: Before top_segment_proportions returns.
checkers.precondition: Finite non-negative matrix, rows with positive total, valid ns. Sparse input is in canonical format; row totals are within the range of the matrix dtype.
checkers.rationale: A cumulative share of counts is a probability mass.
checkers.scientific_quantity: cumulative share of the top genes

checkers.alarm: max difference > (64*(sqrt(n_vars)+log2(n_vars))+4*n_vars)*eps.
checkers.invariant: The proportions of the same matrix do not depend on dense vs CSR storage.
checkers.observation_point: Before top_segment_proportions returns; re-called on the other representation.
checkers.precondition: As SC-QC-001.
checkers.rationale: QC metrics must not depend on matrix storage.
checkers.scientific_quantity: cumulative share of the top genes

checkers.alarm: max difference > (64*(sqrt(n_vars)+log2(n_vars))+4*n_vars)*eps. Integer and bool inputs are promoted to float64 for top_proportions.
checkers.invariant: top_proportions(m, n)[:, k-1] equals top_segment_proportions(m, ns)[:, j] for each k = ns[j] (the same cumulative share of the k most expressed genes).
checkers.observation_point: Before top_segment_proportions returns; top_proportions is called with checking disabled.
checkers.precondition: As SC-QC-001.
checkers.rationale: Two estimators of one quantity must agree.
checkers.scientific_quantity: cumulative share of the top genes

checkers.alarm: |stat(P) - stat| > 64*eps*max(eps_values,eps64)*(1+|mean|/std)*(log2(n)+2+2n/64)*(1+|stat|).
checkers.invariant: Permuting the observations (graph rows and columns together with the values) leaves the statistic unchanged.
checkers.observation_point: After the statistic is computed (up to 4 features); re-called on permuted inputs in the production dtype.
checkers.precondition: Square non-negative finite graph, finite values with positive variance. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Features whose sum of squared deviations is below finfo(float64).tiny/eps (subnormal range) are not judged. The statistic's partial sums stay within the float64 range in every summation order (4*max|x-mean|^2*n*max(1,sum of weights) below finfo(float64).max/2).
checkers.rationale: Spatial autocorrelation cannot depend on the arbitrary order in which cells are stored.

checkers.alarm: |stat(ax+b) - stat(x)| > 64*eps*eps64*(1+(max|x|+|b|)/std)*(log2(n)+2+2n/64)*(1+|stat|).
checkers.invariant: x -> a*x + b (a != 0) leaves the statistic unchanged.
checkers.observation_point: After the statistic is computed; re-called with a=-4 and b a power of two near max|x| against a float64 baseline re-call.
checkers.precondition: As SC-AUT-001, values promoted to float64. Features whose sum of squared deviations is below finfo(float64).tiny/eps are not judged. The transformed statistic must stay within the float64 range (4*(|a|*max|x|+|b|)^2*n*max(1,sum of weights) below finfo(float64).max), and the smallest product of a non-zero weight and the mean squared deviation must be at least finfo(float64).tiny/eps.
checkers.rationale: Both statistics are defined on standardised deviations from the mean.

checkers.alarm: difference > 64*eps*max(eps64,eps_vec)*n*(1+mean^2/var)*(1+|stat|).
checkers.invariant: Vector, dense-matrix row and CSR-matrix row of the same values give the same statistic.
checkers.observation_point: After the statistic is computed; re-called through dense and CSR 2-D representations.
checkers.precondition: Square non-negative finite graph, finite values with positive variance. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). Features whose sum of squared deviations is below finfo(float64).tiny/eps are not judged. The uncentred sparse-kernel expansion stays within the value dtype's range (8*max|x|^2*n*max(1,sum of weights) below finfo(dtype).max/2, dtype at most float64).
checkers.rationale: The result must not depend on the container of the values.

checkers.alarm: |s(A|B) + s(B|A)| > 64*eps*eps32*(1+|s|) or |p - p'| > 64*eps*eps64*N*kappa*(1+|s|).
checkers.invariant: statistic(A vs B) = -statistic(B vs A) and the two-sided p-values agree.
checkers.observation_point: At return of rank_genes_groups; re-called with roles swapped on a copy of the matrix. Genes are matched by column position; when var names are not unique the comparison is made on position-labelled copies.
checkers.precondition: method t-test or wilcoxon, explicit reference, at most 3 compared groups. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). A compared group whose category is literally named 'rest' is not swapped (reference='rest' is the all-other-cells keyword).
checkers.rationale: Swapping the two groups of a two-sample test must negate the statistic.

checkers.alarm: scores or log fold changes differ by > 64*eps*(eps32 + eps64*n_obs*kappa)*(1+|v|) with kappa = 1 + max_gene mean^2/var of the statistics' space (expm1 of the data when mean_in_log_space=False). Log fold changes are compared with an additional allowance for the rest-group mean (computed by subtraction): 64*eps*(log2(n_obs+2)+n_obs/32)*sum|x|/n_rest/(ln2*(|m_rest|+1e-9)); genes where this allowance is >= 0.5 are not judged.
checkers.invariant: Comparing a group to 'rest' and to the other group are the same comparison.
checkers.observation_point: At return of rank_genes_groups; re-called with the other reference form. Genes are matched by column position; when var names are not unique the comparison is made on position-labelled copies.
checkers.precondition: t-test, t-test_overestim_var or wilcoxon; groupby has exactly two populated categories and no NaN labels. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries).
checkers.rationale: With two groups the rest is the other group.

checkers.alarm: |lfc + lfc'| > 64*eps*eps32*(1+|lfc|).
checkers.invariant: lfc(A vs B) = -lfc(B vs A).
checkers.observation_point: At return of rank_genes_groups; re-called with roles swapped. Genes are matched by column position; when var names are not unique the comparison is made on position-labelled copies.
checkers.precondition: method t-test or wilcoxon, explicit reference, at most 3 compared groups. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries). A compared group whose category is literally named 'rest' is not swapped (reference='rest' is the all-other-cells keyword).
checkers.rationale: A log ratio changes sign when its arguments are swapped.

checkers.alarm: A gene whose mean difference exceeds the margin has an lfc of the opposite sign or an lfc of exactly 0.
checkers.invariant: sign(lfc) = sign(mean_group - mean_reference), with means taken in the space the function documents (mean of the data when mean_in_log_space=True, mean of expm1(data) when False); expm1 and the pseudocount are monotone.
checkers.observation_point: At return of rank_genes_groups; means computed from the same data matrix. Genes are matched by column position; when var names are not unique the comparison is made on position-labelled copies.
checkers.precondition: t-test, t-test_overestim_var or wilcoxon; non-negative expression data; finite logfoldchanges; mean difference larger than 64*max(eps_x,eps64)*(|m_g|+|m_r|+1e-9)*(log2(n_obs+2)+n_obs/32) + 1e-8*(|m_g|+|m_r|). Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries).
checkers.rationale: The direction of a fold change must follow the direction of the expression difference.

checkers.alarm: |s(-X) + s(X)| > 64*eps*eps32*(1+|s|) or |p - p'| > 64*eps*eps64*N*kappa*(1+|s|), kappa = 1 + max_gene mean^2/var.
checkers.invariant: statistic(-X) = -statistic(X) and p-values agree.
checkers.observation_point: At return of rank_genes_groups; re-called on a negated copy. Signed-integer data is negated after promotion to float64. Genes are matched by column position; when var names are not unique the comparison is made on position-labelled copies.
checkers.precondition: method wilcoxon, or t-test with mean_in_log_space=True (with False the t statistic is computed on expm1 of the data, which is not odd); data not stored as unsigned integers (negation wraps). Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries).
checkers.rationale: Reversing the order of expression values reverses the direction of a location test.

checkers.alarm: mean difference > 64*eps*max(eps_x,eps64)*(sum_g n_g|m_g|/n_rest+|m|)*(log2(n+2)+n/32) or variance difference > 64*eps*max(eps_x,eps64)*n*(1+m^2/v)*v.
checkers.invariant: means_rest and vars_rest of group g equal the mean and sample variance (ddof=1) of the observations outside g (up to 4 groups checked).
checkers.observation_point: After the rest statistics are derived; compared with fast_array_utils.stats.mean_var on those observations (the checker computes the reference in float64).
checkers.precondition: Vs-rest mode, finite data. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries).
checkers.rationale: The rest group of a differential test must be the cells outside the group.

checkers.alarm: max |score(reversed) - score| > (64*log2(n_vars)+4*n_vars)*max(eps_x,eps64)*max|X|.
checkers.invariant: A gene signature is a set: reordering gene_list (same random state) leaves the scores unchanged.
checkers.observation_point: At return of score_genes; re-called with the reversed list and a copy of the generator state.
checkers.precondition: Any gene_list; rng seed or generator. Gene means do not overflow the dtype (max|X|*n_vars below half the dtype maximum) and the scores are finite.
checkers.rationale: Scores must not depend on the order a user lists genes.

checkers.alarm: max |score(X+c) - score(X)| > (64*log2(n_vars)+4*n_vars)*eps64*(max|X|+c).
checkers.invariant: Adding a constant to all expression values leaves the score unchanged (a difference of means; control bins use ranks).
checkers.observation_point: At return of score_genes; re-called on float64 data and on the same data shifted by c.
checkers.precondition: Finite data; shift c = power of two above max|X|; any two genes whose means agree within max(1e3, 64*log2(n_obs+2)+2*n_obs)*eps*(c+max|X|) (rounding of the n_obs-term gene means of the shifted copy) have identical columns (no rank collision). As SC-SG-001, and the shifted copy stays within the float64 range.
checkers.rationale: A score contrasts a signature with matched controls, so a global offset cancels.

checkers.alarm: A control gene outside gene_pool or inside gene_list.
checkers.invariant: Control genes are drawn from the gene pool and contain no signature gene.
checkers.observation_point: After the control set is built.
checkers.precondition: Any call that returns.
checkers.rationale: A control set that contains the signature (or genes outside the pool) biases the contrast.

checkers.alarm: max |W - W^T| > 64*eps*max(1,max W) or an entry outside [-slack, 1+slack].
checkers.invariant: The connectivity matrix equals its transpose and its finite entries lie in [0,1].
checkers.observation_point: After connectivities are computed.
checkers.precondition: Any method (gauss with 64-bit distances (float64, or integer whose largest square does not exceed the dtype maximum; gauss squares in the input dtype, so larger integer distances wrap) that are symmetric up to rounding on mutually stored pairs, umap, jaccard); non-finite weights (e.g. a zero local scale at duplicate points) are not judged.
checkers.rationale: Connectivities of an undirected neighbour graph are symmetric weights.

checkers.alarm: |SST - (SSW+SSB)| > 64*eps*max(eps64,eps_data)*N*(1+mean^2/var)*SST per gene. The reference is computed in float64.
checkers.invariant: (N-1)*Var_total = sum_g (n_g-1)*Var_g + sum_g n_g*(mean_g - mean)^2 (law of total variance).
checkers.observation_point: Before aggregate_array returns; Var_total from fast_array_utils.stats.mean_var.
checkers.precondition: mean and var requested with dof=1, finite data with max|x|^2*N within the float64 range, >= 3 observations kept; genes whose error bound 64*eps*N*(1+mean^2/var) reaches 1 or whose variance is below finfo(float64).tiny/eps (numerically constant or subnormal) are not judged. Sparse input is in canonical format (no repeated (row, column) entries).
checkers.rationale: Group-wise statistics must reassemble to the overall variance.

checkers.alarm: max |corrected - corrected(reversed)| > 50*1e-4*max|X|.
checkers.invariant: Reordering the batch categories does not change the corrected values (labels are exchangeable); equality holds up to the EB iteration's stopping tolerance (relative change 1e-4 per sweep).
checkers.observation_point: Before combat stores its result; re-called with reversed categories.
checkers.precondition: No covariates, >= 2 batches with >= 2 cells, finite data.
checkers.rationale: Batch names carry no information.

checkers.alarm: relative residual of the within-batch linear fit > 64*eps*(1+|mean_in|/std_in+|mean_out|/std_out)*sqrt(n_batch) or a non-positive slope.
checkers.invariant: Within one batch each gene's corrected values are a positive affine function of its original values (location-scale model).
checkers.observation_point: Before combat stores its result.
checkers.precondition: No covariates; batches with >= 3 cells; genes that are not (numerically) constant within the batch being judged. The within-batch spread of a gene must exceed 64*eps*max|x| of that gene across all batches.
checkers.rationale: ComBat adjusts location and scale per batch and gene; it must not reorder cells within a batch.

checkers.alarm: max |V V^T - I| > 64*eps*eps*n_vars, max |var(score_k) - variance_k| > 64*eps*eps*n_obs*lambda_1, or off-diagonal score covariance / lambda_1 > 64*eps*eps*n_obs/gap.
checkers.invariant: PCs^T PCs = I, scores are uncorrelated (adjacent component gap >= 1e-2*lambda_1), each score variance equals the reported component variance.
checkers.observation_point: Before pca stores its result.
checkers.precondition: zero_center=True, solver arpack/covariance_eigh/full, not chunked, finite data. Total variance is finite and at least finfo(float64).tiny/eps*n_vars. The total variance is at least finfo(dtype).tiny/eps*n_vars for the dtype of the data.
checkers.rationale: These are the defining properties of a PCA.

checkers.alarm: max |variance_ratio - variance/total| > 64*eps*(n_vars*variance_1/total + kappa_tot*(log2(n_obs+2)+n_obs/32+log2(n_vars+2))) with kappa_tot = 1+sum_g mean_g^2/total (per-gene variances accumulate recursively over n_obs cells).
checkers.invariant: variance_ratio_k = variance_k / sum_g Var(X_g) with the total from fast_array_utils.stats.mean_var.
checkers.observation_point: Before pca stores its result.
checkers.precondition: As SC-PCA-001. The reference total variance is computed in float64.
checkers.rationale: The ratio is reported relative to the total variance of the data.
